title: Triumph of the Willful
subtitle: UnitedHealth Group Makes great decisions, thanks to this newsletter. A satirical victory lap.
body_html:
Never, when I began relentlessly making fun of UnitedHealthcare and its parent company, UnitedHealth Group, did I ever imagine I would win. But today, at least according to my Google News alerts and a cursory review of recent earning statements, victory is at hand…

And just as I was about to publish this article, which is satire, I have more breaking news! A “UHC insider” (unconfirmed) contacted me with the following information:

So we will see if this piece of information pans out. But it looks as if United has another reduction in force, on top of the several rounds they had in 2024. My article on the prior round of layoffs at UHC is available here.

Usually, it would be a little bit too cheeky of me to use a “notorious Nazi propagandist” reference as the title of an article, but given the states of “parody” and “reality” are rapidly approaching parity…I think I have cover.

I have a Google news alert set up for UnitedHealth Group, and what hit my inbox amazed me.

The alert? I had to click through. It was a tantalizing surprise:

Right there, in black-and-white, in the pages of the news source for the common man, “managed healthcare executive,” we are brought the breaking news of a vow, presumably taken on pain of death, by noted oath-taker Sir Andrew Witty, the chief executive officer of the largest healthcare company on earth. He has taken a solemn vow to reduce prior authorization… somehow, and—presumably—in some way. these are exciting times.

I am going to pretend this is entirely true, and he totally means that, and, taking one additional flight of fancy, it is 100% due to my mockery both here and on TikTok that this change came about. Join me, dear readers, for a satirical victory lap!

Sir Witty had the following to say:

“People’s health interactions should be as intuitive and seamless as every other aspect of their lives, banking, shopping, streaming,” he said. “This past year, we saw an extraordinary increase in the use of these modern channels. We know there is still a large gap, and we intend to keep at it until it is closed.”

I intend to take Andrew Witty at his word, and I do believe that they're gonna keep at that gap until it's closed; it's the time scale that I'm not entirely clear on. It could take… Any amount of time… which might limit the immediacy of the relief individuals would feel?

Is it at this point that I remind my readers that the name of the United Healthcare subsidiary Optum podcast is "Until It's Fixed.” Again, with a time scale unspecified, but with a solemn vow.

Moving on, since that question doesn't seem particularly important, the crucial thing to realize here is that We Did It. That's the royal We. I mean me. I did it. This newsletter and my funny TikTok videos making fun of United, which I'm sure they've definitely seen, maybe even once. That was the agent of change. Don't believe me? Well, I have a smoking gun; take a look at the next notification in my Google news alerts:

You see, I wrote a bunch of articles about antitrust regulation, and here we are, with the FTC following my lead and United Healthcare backing down. That's what it was, it was me writing funny articles and Lina Khan, I assume, reading them. And then using a Time Machine to investigate the company began before those articles were written. And now United is changing its tune. There's even more data to back up my outrageous claims!

I'm not even gonna read the article. Still, the American Medical Association, in what I assume is a completely off-the-cuff comment in an official press release, states that "it's good news that United healthcare is finally…”

I'm assuming that's the entire article. That one sentence, including the non-conclusion of the sentence, just leaving it at that ”is finally…” is entirety of the press release from the American Medical Association. It's for the best if you don't fact check that assertion. The news doesn't stop there.

United had an earnings call, and I'm sure everything was fine.

2024 revenues of over $400 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $27.66 were well within the outlook ranges we set out over a year ago. To be sure, things played out differently than initially anticipated, but it is an enduring trait of this enterprise that we deliver on our commitments to the people we serve and to you, even amid unforeseen circumstances.

Unforeseen circumstances… like this ruthlessly effective humorist with a tiny subscriber base poking fun at one of the largest companies on earth? Exactly.

It's not like there have been other unforeseen circumstances. I'm sure it has nothing to do with the following movement of the share price…

Nothing to see here, just United Health Group choosing to do the right thing because somebody made some compelling TikTok videos and wrote some satirical articles. Nothing else happened in the world. Nothing of note, no significant changes, nothing to write home about.

O.K., maybe there was an inauguration this week, which may impact public markets. But really, how much does that matter? There are more relevant things in the world, like that time I wrote a parody press release from Sauron and Gollum complaining that United acquired Mordor and shit canned the ring?

That was some A+ material.

Here are some more completely unrelated headlines, other than those bolstered during my argument that I'm right and that I convinced United Healthcare to change their ways!

You see— more lawsuits, as I predicted! There are arguments that the US healthcare industry is flawed in a way that is purposeful, which is precisely what I've been writing about, in a somewhat humorous but much too convoluted format for anyone to bother following, other than the higher-up at United Healthcare, who are completely tuned into everything I'm saying, and finally decided to turn the ship around.

Of course, the last article in my Google News alerts about United Healthcare might be familiar to my readers…

That is right! This newsletter is now index by Google as an actual legitimate new source, so every time I write anything about United healthcare, everybody who's got a Google news alert about it is gonna get my article in their inbox. Welcome to the big time. I am inescapable force. I can only assume that the leadership of United healthcare makes all of their decisions based only on what generate school news alerts, and they didn't wanna have gentle ribbing directed their way from this particular Author. United blinked first.

Andrew Witty, I salute you. Thank you for your Vow to change things for the better, I have no reason to believe that that's not exactly what's going to happen. By the way, thank you for the Christmas present, it was well received by my family.

I presume we'll add more value-based contracting and the CPT codes for fMRI-guided accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation any day now?

Share
